body:
Found the throughput bottleneck: the drain launcher was pinned to a batch that had drained to three

This is the answer to why we have been shipping about one spec an hour, and it is not the implementer and not CI.

My standing launcher was relaunching `queue work --batch followups-0918h`. That batch has three open members left. Meanwhile sixteen specs you approved and routed to role:implementer — the whole followups-0918i wave you groomed, plus BUG-1283 you filed an hour ago — were sitting in the queue untouched, because --batch filters them out before the drain ever looks at the queue. Every wave for hours has been re-driving the same two or three specs, which is also why the last one reported shipped 0, shelved 2.

The queue was nineteen deep and the drain could see three of them.

WHAT I CHANGED, all dispatch rather than disposition, nothing re-groomed:
- Launcher now drives batch followups-0918i, sixteen approved members. Your grooming decided what is in it and what execution_mode each carries; I only pointed the drain at it.
- Added batch:followups-0918i to TASK-1289 (mid rework round 4), TASK-1290, TASK-1294 and TASK-168, with --add-tag, so the in-flight work joins the wave rather than being stranded by the switch. Spot-checked that parent: tags survived.
- Added --steal to the drain command, which is the workaround for the orphaned-lease problem in my previous mail.
- The drain now starts under setsid, so killing the launcher can never again take a live drain and its codex child down with it. That is the TASK-168 failure, fixed at the source rather than apologised for.

TASK-168 still needs your status reset before it can be picked up; it is tagged into the new wave and will be driven the moment it is Approved.

The lesson I am taking from this, since it is the second time this week a filter has silently discarded work: a --batch drain reports what it drained, never what it skipped. If the wave's headline had said "3 members, 16 other approved specs routed to this role are not in this batch", I would have caught it hours ago. Worth a spec if you agree — the drain already has both numbers in hand at start-up.
